## 1. Academic / ArXiv

**No new Hopf fibration or Gauss-map papers in scope this week.** Searches across arXiv and Springer returned nothing from the past 7 days matching "Hopf fibration" + "3D printing" or "Gauss map" + "additive manufacturing." OrientIQ's core mathematical framing remains academically novel in this application domain.

**Background context — recent 2026 papers (not this week, but relevant):**

| Paper | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| "A comprehensive review of support structure minimization in additive manufacturing" — Chaudhary et al., *Springer*, July 2026. [Link](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00170-026-18633-1) | Survey that will be widely cited; validates the problem space orientIQ targets. Doesn't use Hopf reduction. |
| "Multi-objective build orientation and topology optimization for cost and time minimization in fiber-reinforced AM" — *Struct. Multidisc. Optim.*, March 2026. [Link](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00158-026-04255-4) | Simultaneous topology + orientation co-optimization. Adds cost/time objectives beyond overhang. More expensive than orientIQ's approach (requires FEA). Watch this direction. |
| "Build Orientation Optimization Using a Multi-objective Framework for Minimizing Build Time and Surface Roughness of FFF Lattice Parts" — Khan et al., Feb 2026. [Link](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-95-1723-7_42) | Narrows to FFF lattice structures; limited overlap with orientIQ's general-mesh scope. Low threat. |

**Assessment:** Research community is active but converging on topology+orientation co-optimization (requires full FEA, slow) rather than the fast, gradient-based S² approach orientIQ uses. No academic group appears to be exploiting the Hopf fibration reduction.

## 2. Slicer Releases

No auto-orient or support-optimization changelog entries found this week across Cura, PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio, Chitubox, Netfabb, or Materialise Magics.

**State of play for context:**

- **Bambu Studio v2.8.2.61** — most recent build. Auto-orient uses cloud-accelerated geometry analysis, good enough for consumer use, not documented as gradient-based or Pareto-aware. [Forum](https://forum.bambulab.com/t/bambu-studio-v2-6-1-public-beta-is-now-available/251485)
- **PrusaSlicer 2.9.4** stable (March 2026); v3.0 in pre-release. SLA optimize-orientation feature exists but is heuristic-only. [PrusaSlicer forum thread](https://forum.prusa3d.com/forum/prusaslicer/prusaslicer-2-3-0-final-sla-optimise-orientation-behaviour-changed/)
- **Cura 5.11.0** — last updated October 2025; no major orientation work noted. Enterprise 5.11 shipped January 2026.

**Assessment:** Slicer auto-orient remains shallow heuristics (minimize contact area or downward-facing area). None expose a Pareto front or functional surface constraints. The gap orientIQ targets is still open.

## 3. Startups & Commercial Players

**CASTOR Technologies — confirmed shut down.** The Israeli AM decision-support startup filed for court-ordered liquidation in the Tel Aviv District Court (October 2025), citing $2.3M in debt and a broader downturn in industrial AM software demand starting in early 2023. The company officially closed after eight years. Customers included Siemens Energy, Stanley Black & Decker, and Evonik. [3DPrint.com](https://3dprint.com/319042/israeli-3d-printing-software-startup-castor-files-for-liquidation/) / [3D Printing Industry](https://3dprintingindustry.com/news/castor-closes-after-eight-years-as-founder-confirms-companys-end-246199/)  
→ **Opportunity:** CASTOR's enterprise customers are unserved for geometry-based orientation analysis. Worth noting for any business development targeting industrial AM users.

**Atlas 3D / Sunata** — acquired by Siemens in 2019, now inside Xcelerator. No new activity this week. Their TCN (Thermal Circuit Network) approach is metal-AM-specific and thermally driven, not the same problem orientIQ solves. [Background](https://www.tctmagazine.com/additive-manufacturing-3d-printing-news/siemens-acquire-additive-manufacturing-software-atlas3d/)

**AMPower** — no news found this week.
